subject: Weaker daily rhythms carried nearly 2.5 times the dementia risk
script: From Agewell Brief: Weaker daily rhythms carried nearly 2.5 times the dementia risk. New research links weaker daily rhythms to increased dementia risk in older adults. People with weaker circadian rhythms had nearly 2.5 times the dementia risk. Later daily activity peaks were tied to a 45% higher risk. Findings don't prove cause; sleep disorders weren't fully accounted for. Read the full source-linked dispatch and primary study caveats at AgewellBrief.com.
